Subject: POC kickoff recap + data collection ask

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we stay coordinated ahead of the POC kickoff: 

Summary of the POC (3-week trial):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for AcmeCorp customer support summarization pipeline (throughput, latency, quality).
- Success criteria (mutually agreed):
  - Quality: >= 85% on on-targetness (human-rated) across sampled prompts; hallucination rate < 5% on critical fields.
  - Latency: median per-response <= 350ms for 512-token requests under test load.
  - Cost: token cost within the expected range we discussed (approx $0.002/token equivalent).

Immediate asks from AcmeCorp (we discussed during the call):
1) Provide a representative prompt set (customer queries / logs) — target 200-300 prompts for the full POC. We can start with an initial batch (50–100) for the first evaluation run. Use the attached template (poc-prompt-collection-template.csv) to map prompts to intent, priority, and any expected-answer examples.
2) Provide a sample of production logs (anonymized) so we can reproduce formatting edge cases (attachments, markdown, long threads).
3) Identify owners: who at AcmeCorp will provide the prompts/logs and who is the approver for success criteria?

Proposed timeline:
- Jan 18–22: Data collection + anonymization (Acme owns)
- Jan 24: Kickoff + data handoff call (technical sync)
- Jan 25–Feb 11: POC runs + periodic check-ins (weekly)
- Feb 14: Final review & next steps

Attachments: poc-prompt-collection-template.csv (attached)

Next steps for today: Sam / Priya — please send an initial batch of 50–100 prompts and one sample logs file (can be anonymized/PII-masked). If you need a scrub checklist, we can share one.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the kickoff invite once we confirm Jan 24.

Subject: Re: POC kickoff recap + data collection ask — technical questions

Thanks for the context — quick technical clarifications from the infra/SE side so we can prepare the eval harness: 

1) File formats: CSV for prompt/expected-answer pairs is ideal (UTF-8). For logs, JSONL is perfect; include one event per line and a field that maps to the user-visible prompt.
2) Anonymization: please remove or hash PII (names, emails, phone numbers). If redaction is tricky, we can run a redaction pass on our side if you provide a sample and confirm ownership/approval.
3) Expected-answer format: both full-text examples and short label(s) are useful. For the primary eval we will compute both semantic similarity (embedding-based) and a human-rated on-targetness score. If you can include a small set (~20) of gold responses that will speed up the human eval calibration.
4) Metrics we will report: on-targetness (human-rated), exact-match for structured fields, hallucination rate (human-rated), latency distribution (p50/p90), and token/cost estimates.
5) Data security: please let us know if logs contain customer-identifiable data; we will enable encrypted S3 transfer and limit retention in the POC environment to 30 days.

I attached a draft POC eval plan (poc-eval-plan.docx) to show the exact fields we need and the proposed evaluation cadence.

If everyone is aligned, I’ll spin up the eval harness once we have the first batch of prompts.

—
